content.title: Snow & Ice Control
content.summary: The City of Arvada prioritizes snow and ice control by plowing and applying de-icing materials to two main routes: Priority 1 for essential streets and Priority 2 for neighborhood collectors. Residential streets are typically not plowed unless declared a snow emergency, but residents can request plowing or ice removal for Priority routes by calling the Street Division. The Colorado Department of Transportation is responsible for plowing certain state highways within the city.
content.body:
The City of Arvada's Snow and Ice control policy is to plow and apply de-icing material to two priority routes. For information about parks and trails, visit the [Parks / Trails Snow Plow Routes](/565/Snow-Plow-Park-Trails-Routes).

## Snow plow routes

### **Priority 1 (red routes)**

These are main, arterial streets, essential streets for emergency vehicle response, school zone streets and streets that provide connectivity with plowed streets in adjoining jurisdictions.

### **Priority 2 (blue routes)**

These are major and minor neighborhood collector streets that provide access from Priority 1 streets to residential streets.

The Priority 1 and 2 streets are shown on the City snow plowing route map. Residential streets are not routinely plowed unless they have steep hills with chronic icing problems. However, they will be plowed if the City Manager declares a snow emergency.

### **CDOT (purple routes)**

The Colorado Department of Transportation (CDOT) is responsible for plowing Wadsworth (SH121), Sheridan (SH95), Highway 93 (SH 93), and Ward Road (SH72) from I-70 to 64th Avenue; 64th Avenue (SH72) from Ward Rd to Indiana St; Indiana St. (SH72) from 64th Avenue to 86th Pkwy; Highway 72 (SH72) from Indiana St. to Highway 119.

         

[The interactive map can also be viewed in a separate window.](https://arvada.maps.arcgis.com/apps/instant/sidebar/index.html?appid=398b509cd3e84fe7b3f5d8256ee82781)

## Requests for plowing and gutter ice removal

To request plowing service on a Priority 1 or 2 route, or if you have a severe ice build-up problem in the street or gutter due to melting snow and ice, you may submit a request by calling the Street Division at 720-898-7725.

Please leave a brief message stating your request and the location - by address or reference to cross streets. Your request will be logged into our work order system.

**Please note:** the City does not remove packed snow and ice from residential streets that are passable by passenger cars.

Listen to the Inside Arvada podcast episode about snow operations using the player above or wherever you listen to podcasts, including [Buzzsprout](https://www.buzzsprout.com/2320363/episodes/16143076-inside-arvada-s-snow-operations-with-keith-bohan)(with transcript).

### [FAQs](/Faq.aspx?TID=77)

[What streets does the City plow?](#)
:   The City prioritizes the most trafficked streets for plowing. This includes main, arterial roads (like 80th or Carr), collector roads that run through neighborhoods, and school zones. This helps ensure commonly used roads remain passable for the traveling public and emergency response teams. Other benefits include:

    - Resource management (keeping costs of equipment, materials, and staff hours relatively stable each year)
    - Reduced disruption on residential streets (snowplow noise and traffic, piles of snow, and treatment materials)

    Additional roads may be plowed when a storm reaches a certain caliber, typically 12 inches of snow or more. At the discretion of City management, additional contractors can be brought in to help plow more roads to ensure safety for the traveling public.

    View the [map of snow plow routes](https://arvada.maps.arcgis.com/apps/instant/sidebar/index.html?appid=398b509cd3e84fe7b3f5d8256ee82781) for more details.

[What streets are plowed by CDOT?](#)
:   State highways like Wadsworth (HWY 121), Sheridan (HWY 95), and parts of Indiana and Ward (HWY 72) are plowed by CDOT (Colorado Department of Transportation). View the [map of snow plow routes](https://arvada.maps.arcgis.com/apps/instant/sidebar/index.html?appid=398b509cd3e84fe7b3f5d8256ee82781) for more details.

[Can I report icing problems in my neighborhood?](#)
:   Yes, to report ice build ups on the road or in gutters please call 720-898-7725. Please leave a brief message with your request and the location by address or cross streets.  Your request will be logged into the work order system to be addressed.

    **Please note:**packed snow and ice on residential roads (outside of [designated plow routes](/503/Snow-Ice-Control)) will not be removed if they are still passable by cars.

[How do I report unshoveled sidewalks?](#)
:   Sidewalks are the responsibility of the home or business owner. [City Code 18-491-302.3.3](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=PTIICOOR_CH18BUBURE_ARTXIINPRMACO_S18-491I.SE302.3.3SNREGE) requires sidewalks to be shoveled within 24 hours after the snow stops. Please report unshoveled sidewalks to code enforcement via [Ask Arvada](https://www.arvadaco.gov/898/Report-a-Problem-or-Ask-a-Question) or by calling 720-898-7465 during regular business hours. Visit the [Shoveling Walkways webpage](https://www.arvadaco.gov/411/Municipal-Code-for-Shoveling-Walkways) for more information.

[Can the City plow my child's school bus stop or route?](#)
:   The City's plow routes include school zones but not all school bus stops or bus routes. These can change at the discretion of the school district and aren't managed by the City. School bus routes therefore cannot be consistently reflected in our route mapping.

[How do I sign up for alerts about a winter weather emergency?](#)
:   Sign up for [Lookout Alerts](https://www.smart911.com/smart911/ref/reg.action?pa=LookoutAlert) to receive alerts in the case of a weather related emergency, including winter weather.

    The [Boulder/Denver sector of the National Weather Service](https://www.weather.gov/bou/) will provide the most accurate information on the status of winter weather events impacting Arvada. The City routinely re-shares their social media posts on [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/cityofarvada) and [X (Twitter)](https://twitter.com/cityofarvada) during storms.

[What materials are used to treat roads during a storm?](#)
:   Before a storm anti-icing salt brine (salt water mixture) can be applied to help prevent snow from sticking. This is only used during some storms as it is not useful if the ground is too warm. During a storm 3 de-icing materials are used based on ground temperatures:

    - Rock (white/gray) salt is used when ground temperatures are near 15 to 20 degrees or above.
    - Blue salt is used when ground temperatures are 0 degrees and above.
    - The liquid material is used when temperatures are below zero.

    All of these materials are industry standard and considered environmentally safe.

[Can I get help shoveling my sidewalks?](#)
:   The City coordinates a Snow Buddies Program to match those who are physically unable to remove snow with volunteers to assist them. Please visit the [Snow Buddies Program page for information](https://www.arvadaco.gov/486/Snow-Buddies-Program) and eligibility requirements. You can also call 720-898-7535 to apply for assistance by phone.

[What about park and trail plowing?](#)
:   The Parks Department is responsible for clearing nearly 150 miles of trails, sidewalks, and parking lots across the city during a snowstorm. There are three categories of routes, prioritized by safety.

    - **Priority 1 Routes** are cleared first; these are trails connecting to schools and recreation centers.
    - **Priority 2 Routes** are cleared second; these are primary use trails and system trails.
    - **Priority 3 Routes** are cleared third; these are secondary use parks, internal and secondary trails.

    [Visit the Parks and Trails Snow Clearing page](https://www.arvadaco.gov/565/Snow-Plow-Park-Trails-Routes) for more information, including an interactive map of the three priority routes.
